entity.current_state: Basic authentication is disabled in all tenants for the affected protocols; applications must use Modern authentication or another supported method.
known_unknowns: The service-wide disablement was phased across tenants and cloud environments, so October 1, 2022 is recorded as the main rollout boundary rather than a fabricated universal completion date.
entity.notes: Current Microsoft documentation confirms the present all-tenants disabled state.
entity.still_usable_note: Microsoft states that Basic authentication is now disabled in all tenants for the affected Exchange Online protocols. Disablement was phased, so this record does not invent one universal final-completion date.
entity.summary: Microsoft removed Basic authentication from affected Exchange Online protocols and requires Modern authentication/OAuth-based access instead.

events.migration_path: Update affected Exchange Online clients and applications to Modern authentication/OAuth 2.0 or supported newer interfaces.
events.notes: October 1, 2022 is the documented main disablement boundary, not an inferred universal final-completion date.
events.summary: Microsoft began permanently disabling Basic authentication in Exchange Online tenants from October 1, 2022 for the affected protocols, with later phased completion across tenants and environments.
events.title: Exchange Online Basic authentication permanent disablement rollout begins
events.user_impact: Applications that depended on username/password Basic authentication for affected Exchange Online protocols must change authentication or stop working.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Microsoft states that Basic authentication is now disabled in all tenants for the affected Exchange Online protocols and documents the phased disablement that began from the October 2022 boundary.
evidence.title: Deprecation of Basic authentication in Exchange Online
